en: The Hymn to the Aśvattha Tree
Śrī Nārada said: "O Grandfather, tell me that one [means] by which this world may effortlessly attain all desires,
and which is the single essence of all the gods."
Brahmā said:
Listen, O divine sage, to [the account of] the Aśvattha tree, which is pure and the soul of all;
by circumambulating it, the world attains all desires.
Rudra is situated to the south of the Aśvattha tree, Viṣṇu resides to the west,
Brahmā is located in the northern region, and Indra and the other deities are in the east.
O bull among sages, cows, Brahmins, and ascetics are situated upon the leaves of the trunk and its branches; the Vedas are the root, and sacrifices are the milk.
Rivers, streams, lakes, and oceans flow from it toward the eastern and other directions;
therefore, a wise person should take refuge in the Aśvattha tree with every effort.
O cool tree, you indeed possess cooling fruit;
by propitiating you, a person shall obtain the fruits pertaining to both this world and the next.
Homage again and again to the Bodhisattva, the divine Aśvattha tree, who always provides refuge for Viṣṇu and whose leaves are ever-moving.
O Aśvattha, King of Trees, since Nārāyaṇa dwells within you at all times,
you are therefore renowned among trees as eternally blessed and the destroyer of misfortune.
O lord of trees, by that same truth through which you are a giver of milk here and by which Fortune attends upon you, may Fortune attend upon me as well.
You are Rudra, the eleven-fold self; you are the crest-jewel of the lords of the Vasus;
you are Nārāyaṇa among the gods; and you are the Pippala, the king of trees.
O you who contain fire within, who contain the *śamī* tree within, who contain the gods within, O Prajāpati;
O Hiraṇyagarbha, Bhūgarbha, and Yajñagarbha—salutations be unto you!
O Lord of the Forest, grant us long life, strength, fame, splendor, progeny, cattle, wealth, sacred knowledge, wisdom, and intelligence.
May Varuṇa protect you constantly; may a favorable gaze rest upon you;
may grasses surround you on all sides; may there be happiness for you.
O Lord Aśvattha, pacify the twitching of the eyes, the twitching of the arms, bad dreams, evil thoughts, and the rising up of enemies.
Salutations to the most excellent Aśvattha, the bestower of all sovereignty;
salutations to the destroyer of evil dreams and the giver of the fruits of auspicious dreams.
Salutations to you, the king of trees, who in your roots has the form of Brahmā, in your middle the form of Viṣṇu, and at your summit the form of Śiva.
I bow to that Aśvattha tree, by seeing which one is freed from diseases, by touching which one is liberated from sins, and by taking refuge in which one becomes long-lived.
O Aśvattha, highly fortunate one, blessed and pleasant to behold!
Grant me my desired objects and bring about the defeat of my enemies.
O God, Great Tree, grant me long life, progeny, wealth, grain, good fortune, and all prosperity; I have come to you for refuge.
Consisting of the mantras of the Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāma Vedas, possessing all forms, and higher than the highest,
this Aśvattha tree, whose root is the Veda, is always proclaimed by the sages.
Even a slayer of a Brahmin, a slayer of a guru, one who is impoverished, or one afflicted by disease,
shall become happy by reciting this hymn one hundred thousand times.
A student of sacred knowledge (brahmacārī), eating sacrificial food (haviṣya), sleeping on the ground, and having conquered his senses—
even one whose mind is afflicted by sin— should observe this vow.
One should prepare a plastering of cow dung measuring one cubit or two cubits,
and worship it especially with the Puruṣasūkta and the Praṇava.
Remaining silent, one should perform circumambulation; thus one shall become a partaker of the fruits previously described.
Indeed, by chanting the thousand names of Viṣṇu, as well as those of Acyuta, [the same result is attained].
Moving from one spot to another without any movement of the hands,
with speech offering praise and the mind in meditation— this is the four-limbed circumambulation.
By him by whom an *aśvattha* tree is planted, his lineage is thereby established;
through the abundance of wealth and longevity, he shall deliver his ancestors from hell.
By taking refuge at the root of an Aśvattha tree and giving vegetables, food, and water,
when a single Brahmin is fed, it is equivalent to feeding ten million Brahmins.
By taking refuge at the root of an aśvattha tree and performing recitation, fire-offerings, and worship of the gods, one obtains imperishable fruit; such is the word of Brahmā.
Thus consoled, the aśvattha tree becomes capable of providing constant consolation;
for when an aśvattha is cut down for the sake of a sacrifice, one shall attain imperishable heaven.
By him who has cut down the Ashvattha tree in vain, the ancestors and deities have been destroyed;
but where the Ashvattha is honored, all the deities are honored.
Thus ends the hymn to the Aśvattha tree.
